newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: AIDS spreading fast among Central America's poor.
newsitem.headline: AIDS spreading fast among Central America's poor.

text.p: AIDS is spreading rapidly among Central America's poor and could reach African proportions in the coming years, experts said on Wednesday.
The experts attending a conference on AIDS in Central America said the virus had taken root in the region's sprawling shantytowns and rural regions.

Ricardo Calderon, Latin American director of the U.S.-based AIDS Control and Prevention Project, said the disease had shifted from upper and middle-class gay men to the region's poor and heterosexual population, a development he termed the "pauperization" of AIDS in Central America.
"We are perhaps five or 10 years behind Africa in terms of the disease's development ... we are going to start to see similar situations in the decade after the year 2000," Calderon told Reuters.

Dr. Fernando Zacarias, regional coordinator of the Pan-American Health Organisation's AIDS programme, said the poor were at higher risk because they lacked decent medical care, nutrition and often the money to buy a condom.
"The region's health systems don't have enough penicillin to treat syphilis. They are not going to be able to deal with AIDS without national and international help," he said.
Central America had 11,142 reported cases of AIDS as of Dec. 10, according to a Pan-American Health Organisation report, which acknowledged massive underreporting.
From 1991 to 1995, the number of new AIDS cases per year doubled to about 2,000 cases per year, the report showed.
The report listed Honduras with 5,666 cases, El Salvador with 1,629, Guatemala with 1,371, Panama with 1,186, Costa Rica with 1,012, Nicaragua with 140 and Belize with 138.
